object: FIELD packet reducer / usable batch loop
host_delta: Turn the existing pure packet reducer into a batchable command-line instrument that can sweep files or directories, emit one exclusive egress class per packet, and summarize counts without creating a queue, store, planner, or new authority source.
laws: THE REDUCER CLASSIFIES; IT DOES NOT PRIORITIZE OR EXECUTE.
NOW STILL REQUIRES EXPLICIT CALLER CONTEXT.
BATCHING DOES NOT CREATE PERSISTENT STATE.
DIRECTORY SWEEP IS A VIEW OVER SOURCE PACKETS, NOT A CANONICAL PACKET STORE.
ONE PACKET -> EXACTLY ONE OF NOW / DELTA / RESIDUE / GATE / NEXT / ARCHIVE.
verify: node tools/field-egress-sweep-selftest.mjs  # fixture + actual control/packets smoke; no-context shelf must emit zero NOW
CI: public-surface-check / Validate JIT FIELD handoff compiler runs both reducer and sweep selftests
residue: The sweep does not infer CURRENT priority.
It does not execute NEXT or mutate source packets.
A later host may consume JSON output, but that consumer must retain native authority and RETURN.
The actual control/packets shelf is exercised by the selftest; Markdown is ignored, JSON packet shapes may differ, and no-context sweep must emit zero NOW.
stop: Do not add another reducer surface. Extend only for a concrete consumer incompatibility or falsified batch invariant.
corrections: Exact-head CI exposed ambiguous variadic context flags: --selected next-c <dir> consumed <dir> as another ID and left no source path. Context flags are now repeatable single-ID flags, so caller authority cannot swallow packet inputs.
